questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly, the city. Secondly, the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat difficult at times. The university's webpage is quite outdated and it is a very different system from what I am used to. But my coordinator has been so very helpful when I have been struggling.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A handful of welcome/information meetings on zoom

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and found it rather quickly through a Facebook group for Danes in Berlin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive (not surprisingly). The large Facebook groups with housing in the city are filled with scammers. Start looking early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Do not know

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online course catalogue. Very outdated webpage and system. It took a looong time. Not only in terms of scrolling, but also in regard to achieving the ECTS points I needed, not being let in immediately and having to show up to classes, write professors, etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My coordinator and a written guide for international students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly succesful. I was able to sign up for the most that I wanted, with one or two exceptions.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience. Ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was appropriate

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It has been very different. There is a lot more class discussion, student activities, turning work in before every class. There is nothing wrong with that style of teaching, but it is more demanding and especially when having five courses on the schedule.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Social Inequalities
An Immigrant Story
Intro to STS
Anthropological Perspectives on Material Culture
Minds and Machines

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course Introduction to Social Inequalities has been very informative and challenging at the same time. If one is interested in courses from sociology and curious to learn how to read texts from this field of study, I highly recommend it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student sports programmes, erasmus events like walks, tours, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Signing up for a sport. There are so many options and it is very fairly priced.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I have found it easier to socialize with local students when there has been activities out of the classroom. Activities outside such as tours, museum visits, etc., are already a fun acitivity in itself but it is also easier and feels more natural to socialize for me at least.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Lack of digitalization and when it is there, it's quite outdated and complicated

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared for a heavy workload if you need to receive 30 ECTS.
2. Take 10 deep breaths when dealing with AGNES.
3. Ask for help! Sooner rather than later. The staff is very helpful here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not any I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Having the opportunity to participate in courses I wouldn't normally have had the chance to necessarily, such as sociology courses. 

I believe in myself more, that I can do things even when they are difficult, hard and complicated. This has been very rewarding and important for me, and it is something that will be helpful throughout my life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving away and doing something very different. Simple answer, but 'just the doing it' has been a challenge, but rewarding in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
